title: AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler
summary: Core compilation pipeline architecture for industrial multi-table data ingestion, schema unification, and deterministic join graphs.

sections.heading_text: Industrial Data Ingestion, Understanding, Unification and Compilation Engine
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > Industrial Data Ingestion, Understanding, Unification and Compilation Engine
sections.content: Project: AI-ConneXPlatform: Industrial AI Solutions PlatformModule: Data StudioComponent: CompilerDocument: Technical R&D and Stage-1 Engineering DocumentationStage: Chatbot → Data Studio Compiler → Data ProfilerDocument Version: 1.0Date: 14 August 2026Status: Architecture / R&D Baseline

The AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler is the first machine-processing layer after the AI-ConneX conversational interface.

Its purpose is to eliminate one of the largest barriers between industrial data and artificial intelligence:

Industrial users should not have to understand data engineering, file formats, schemas, joins, merges, encoding, or data normalization before using AI-ConneX.

Industrial data is rarely delivered in a clean, standardized form.

A plant may provide:

CSV files

Excel workbooks

JSON

XML

Parquet

TXT/log files

database exports

ZIP archives

multiple files from multiple machines

historical files

files with different column names

files with different timestamps

files containing different units

datasets containing overlapping records

datasets that need to be appended

datasets that need to be joined

datasets that need to be merged

datasets containing metadata and operational measurements together

The Compiler receives this heterogeneous input and converts it into a validated AI-ConneX Unified Industrial Dataset representation.

The Compiler does not simply convert:

Excel → CSV

or:

ZIP → extracted files

Instead, it performs:

INGEST   ↓IDENTIFY   ↓INSPECT   ↓PROFILE PRE-CHECK   ↓UNDERSTAND   ↓PLAN   ↓UNZIP / EXTRACT   ↓NORMALIZE   ↓JOIN / APPEND / MERGE   ↓SCHEMA HARMONIZATION   ↓TYPE / TIME / UNIT ALIGNMENT   ↓VALIDATION   ↓PROVENANCE   ↓UNIFIED DATASET   ↓DATA PROFILER

The Compiler is assisted by an Agent Helper.

The Agent Helper does not directly manipulate production data without controls.

Its primary responsibility is:

Understand ambiguous industrial datasets and recommend the correct transformation plan.

The Compiler then validates and executes the plan deterministically.

Therefore the architecture follows:

Agent reasons     ↓Compiler validates     ↓Compiler executes     ↓Validator verifies     ↓Profiler receives result

This separation is fundamental to the reliability of AI-ConneX.

sections.heading_text: 2. Position of the Compiler in AI-ConneX
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 2. Position of the Compiler in AI-ConneX
sections.content:
The relevant section of the AI-ConneX architecture is:

JANE / CHATBOT                              │                              │                              ▼                    ┌───────────────────┐                    │   DATA STUDIO     │                    │                   │                    │     COMPILER      │                    └─────────┬─────────┘                              │                    Unified Industrial                         Dataset                              │                              ▼                    ┌───────────────────┐                    │   DATA PROFILER   │                    └─────────┬─────────┘                              │                              ▼                    Recipe Orchestrator                              │                              ▼                        DAG Assigner

The Compiler is therefore the boundary between human/industrial intent and structured machine-readable data.

Without AI-ConneX:

Industrialist      ↓Finds data      ↓Calls data engineer      ↓Converts Excel      ↓Unzips files      ↓Checks schemas      ↓Renames columns      ↓Writes Python/Pandas code      ↓Joins datasets      ↓Fixes timestamps      ↓Handles missing values      ↓Exports clean dataset      ↓ML engineer receives dataset

This creates several problems.

Industrial personnel may understand:

machines

production

maintenance

process parameters

plant operations

but may not understand:

Python

Pandas

SQL

schemas

ETL

joins

data types

encodings
Industrial data can arrive in arbitrary formats.

Two datasets may represent the same concept using different names.

Example:

Machine_IDmachine_idmachineasset_idequipment_no

The system must determine whether datasets should be:

APPENDEDJOINEDMERGEDLEFT JOINEDAS-OF JOINEDUNIONED

Industrial datasets frequently contain:

UTC

local time

date only

timestamp

epoch time

different timestamp resolutions

For example:

temperature = °Ctemperature = °Fpressure = barpressure = psi

A simple schema match is insufficient.
The Compiler has six primary objectives.
Accept heterogeneous industrial file formats.
Determine what each file/dataset contains.

Determine whether datasets should be:

appended

joined

merged

left/right/full joined

time-aligned

unioned
Convert the resulting dataset into the AI-ConneX canonical representation.
Prevent incorrect transformations from silently entering ML pipelines.
Maintain the lineage of every important transformation.

The AI-ConneX Compiler can be formally defined as:

A schema-aware, provenance-preserving industrial data compilation engine that transforms heterogeneous user-provided datasets into a validated canonical representation suitable for downstream data profiling, feature engineering and machine-learning workflows.

It is therefore an ETL/ELT + schema inference + data reasoning + validation engine.

The most important rule is:

LLM / Agent ≠ Data Executor

The Agent Helper should not be trusted to arbitrarily execute transformations.

Instead:

User Intent    ↓Agent Helper    ↓Transformation Proposal    ↓Compiler Validation    ↓Deterministic Executor    ↓Validation    ↓Output

This protects industrial data from uncontrolled agent behavior.
The R&D process should be divided into the following phases.
Determine the formats that industrial users are likely to provide.
CSVXLSXXLSMJSONXMLTXTLOGPARQUETZIP
PDF tablesAvroORCSQLiteSQL dumpsAPI responsesS3 objectsindustrial databasesOPC-UA exportsMQTT data snapshotsSCADA exportsMES exportsERP exports

The system should never trust the filename extension alone.

For example:

machine.csv

may actually contain:

semicolon-separated data

or:

UTF-16 encoded data

or even malformed binary content.

The Compiler therefore performs:

filename inspection+MIME detection+magic-byte detection+parser probing

The detected type is stored separately from the supplied filename.

ZIP files are particularly important because industrialists frequently send:

plant_data.zip

rather than individual files.

The Compiler therefore needs:

ZIP detection     ↓safe extraction     ↓recursive file discovery     ↓file classification     ↓dataset grouping

A naive implementation might execute:

zipfile.extractall(output_directory)

without checking archive paths.

This can create a Zip Slip/path traversal vulnerability.

A malicious archive could contain:

../../some_sensitive_file

The Compiler must therefore resolve every archive member and verify that the final extraction path remains inside the designated workspace.

Another failure is a compressed archive that is tiny but expands to enormous size.

Example:

Input ZIP:50 MBExpanded:500 GB

Without controls, the server could run out of:

disk

RAM

CPU

worker capacity

The Compiler must implement:

maximum archive sizemaximum uncompressed sizemaximum file countmaximum nesting depthmaximum individual file size

After files are identified, the Compiler creates a discovery report.

Example:

{  "dataset_id": "DS-000184",  "file": "machine_data.csv",  "format": "csv",  "encoding": "utf-8",  "delimiter": ",",  "rows_estimate": 1845023,  "columns": 17,  "has_header": true,  "timestamp_candidates": [    "timestamp",    "event_time"  ],  "identifier_candidates": [    "machine_id"  ]}

This is not yet the final Data Profiler output.

It is a Compiler discovery artifact.
Suppose the user gives:
machine_idtimestamptemperaturepressure

MachineTimeTempPressure

A naive system sees different schemas.

AI-ConneX must infer:

machine_id ←→ Machinetimestamp  ←→ Timetemperature ←→ Temppressure ←→ Pressure

The Agent Helper assists in this process.

Schema matching should use multiple signals.

Schema Match                         │        ┌────────────────┼─────────────────┐        ▼                ▼                 ▼     Name           Data Type          Values   Similarity        Similarity        Similarity        │                │                 │        └────────────────┼─────────────────┘                         ▼                  Semantic Score

Potential scoring:

column_name_similarity+datatype_similarity+sample_value_similarity+unit_similarity+semantic_embedding_similarity+timestamp compatibility+domain vocabulary

The final result should be a confidence score.

The Agent Helper is the intelligent reasoning component.

It receives:

dataset metadata+schemas+sample values+column statistics+user objective+known industrial vocabulary

It produces:

transformation proposal+confidence+reason+required keys+warnings

Example:

{  "operation": "JOIN",  "left": "machine_data",  "right": "production_data",  "keys": [    "machine_id",    "timestamp"  ],  "join_type": "LEFT",  "confidence": 0.94,  "reason": "Both datasets share machine identifier and compatible timestamps."}

The Compiler should prefer APPEND when:

schemas are substantially compatibleANDrecords represent different partitions/time periodsANDno complementary-key relationship is required

Example:

Jan.csvFeb.csvMar.csv

becomes:

Jan +Feb +Mar ↓APPEND

JOIN is appropriate when datasets contain complementary attributes.

Example:

Machine:machine_id | timestamp | temperatureProduction:machine_id | timestamp | production_rate

Output:

machine_idtimestamptemperatureproduction_rate

MERGE should be used when overlapping datasets require reconciliation.

For example:

Machine A:machine_id | temperature | pressureMachine B:machine_id | temperature | vibration

The Compiler may produce:

machine_idtemperaturepressurevibration

But if both datasets contain different values for the same field, the conflict must be recorded rather than silently overwritten.

A major R&D failure mode is an incorrect join.

Example:

Dataset A:

machine_id = M01

appears 100,000 times.

Dataset B:

machine_id = M01

appears 50,000 times.

Joining only on:

machine_id

can potentially create billions of combinations.

This is a many-to-many join explosion.

The Compiler should therefore estimate join cardinality before execution.

Expected join size        ↓Risk estimation        ↓If excessive        ↓Reject / require confirmation

Industrial data may contain:

2026-08-14 10:00:00

while another dataset contains:

14/08/2026 10:00

and another:

1723636200

The Compiler should normalize these into a canonical timestamp representation.

Recommended internal representation:

UTC timestamp+original timezone+original timestamp

Do not discard the original value.

Consider:

Sensor:1-second intervals

and:

Production:1-hour intervals

A normal equality join will fail.

The Compiler should detect granularity differences and potentially recommend:

AS-OF JOINWINDOW JOINRESAMPLINGAGGREGATION

rather than forcing equality.

Example:

Dataset A:temperature = °CDataset B:temperature = °F

The column names are identical.

A purely schema-based Compiler would incorrectly treat them as identical.

Therefore the Compiler must consider:

semantic meaning+unit+value distribution

before combining them.

Industrial files may use:

UTF-8UTF-8 BOMUTF-16Latin-1Windows-1252

The Compiler should attempt safe encoding detection and record:

original_encodingdetected_encodingconversion_applied

CSV is deceptively difficult.

Potential problems:

,;|\t

Different delimiters may be used.

Fields may contain:

"Machine, Line 1"

without being correctly escaped.

The Compiler should detect:

delimiterquote characterescape characterheaderencodingline ending

before parsing.

Industrial Excel workbooks may contain:

multiple sheets

hidden sheets

merged cells

header rows beginning at row 5

notes above the table

multiple tables on one sheet

formulas

macros

blank rows

inconsistent columns

The Compiler therefore needs an Excel discovery stage:

Workbook   ↓Sheet discovery   ↓Table-region detection   ↓Header detection   ↓Schema extraction

JSON can represent:

array of objects

or:

nested objects

or:

deeply nested telemetry

Example:

{  "machine": {    "id": "M01",    "telemetry": {      "temperature": 72.4    }  }}

The Compiler needs a controlled flattening strategy.

It must not arbitrarily flatten every nested structure because hierarchy can contain meaning.

Industrial systems frequently exchange XML-like structured data.

Potential problems:

namespaces

deeply nested structures

malformed XML

external entity attacks

enormous XML expansion

The parser should therefore use secure XML parsing practices.

A column may contain:

123N/A4

The parser may infer it as:

string

instead of:

integer

The Compiler should perform type inference with explicit handling of:

nullmissingNAN/Aunknown-error

Two files may contain overlapping records.

Example:

January.csvJanuary_backup.csv

Appending both creates duplicate records.

The Compiler should calculate duplicate signatures using candidate keys such as:

machine_id+timestamp+measurement

where appropriate.

It should distinguish:

exact duplicate

from:

legitimate repeated observation

Industrial systems evolve.

Version 1:

temperaturepressure

Version 2:

temperaturepressurevibration

Version 3:

temp_cpressure_barvibration_mm_s

The Compiler should not treat this as an error automatically.

It should detect:

schema version change

and create a harmonization plan.

tables:
| Failure Class | Risk | Compiler Solution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unknown file type | High | MIME + signature + parser probing |
| ZIP traversal | Critical | Safe extraction validation |
| ZIP bomb | Critical | Expansion limits |
| Huge CSV | High | Streaming/chunked processing |
| Wrong delimiter | Medium | Delimiter detection |
| Encoding mismatch | Medium | Encoding detection |
| Header not first row | Medium | Header inference |
| Different column names | High | Semantic schema matching |
| Wrong join type | Critical | Agent proposal + cardinality validation |
| Join explosion | Critical | Cardinality estimation |
| Duplicate records | High | Duplicate analysis |
| Timestamp mismatch | High | Timestamp normalization |
| Timezone mismatch | High | UTC canonicalization |
| Unit mismatch | Critical | Unit detection/conversion |
| Data type mismatch | High | Type inference + coercion policy |
| Nested JSON | Medium | Controlled flattening |
| XML attack | Critical | Secure parser |
| Schema drift | High | Schema versioning |
| Conflicting values | High | Conflict detection |
| Missing keys | High | Join-key quality assessment |
| Corrupt files | Medium | Quarantine + diagnostics |
| Malicious content | Critical | Sandbox/isolation |
| Agent hallucination | Critical | Structured plan + deterministic execution |
| LLM unavailable | Medium | Rule-based fallback |
| LLM wrong recommendation | Critical | Confidence threshold + validation |

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 33. How AI-ConneX Overcomes Agent Errors
sections.content:
The Agent Helper must never be the final authority.

Architecture:

AGENT HELPER                     │                     ▼             Proposed Plan                     │                     ▼              PLAN VALIDATOR                     │        ┌────────────┼─────────────┐        ▼            ▼             ▼     Schema       Cardinality     Units     Check          Check         Check        │            │             │        └────────────┼─────────────┘                     ▼              EXECUTION ENGINE                     │                     ▼              RESULT VALIDATOR

This provides a safety boundary around the LLM.

Recommended policy:

Confidence >= 0.90    → automatic execution0.75–0.89    → execution with warning / optional confirmation0.50–0.74    → ask user or perform additional analysis< 0.50    → do not execute

For high-risk transformations, confidence alone should not be enough.

Example:

Potential many-to-many JOIN

should require explicit validation even if the Agent reports high confidence.

The Compiler should transform the Agent’s recommendation into a deterministic recipe.

Example:

{  "recipe_version": "1.0",  "operations": [    {      "id": "op01",      "type": "UNZIP",      "input": "upload_001"    },    {      "id": "op02",      "type": "APPEND",      "inputs": [        "machine_01.csv",        "machine_02.csv"      ]    },    {      "id": "op03",      "type": "JOIN",      "left": "op02",      "right": "production.xlsx",      "keys": [        "machine_id",        "timestamp"      ],      "join_type": "LEFT"    }  ]}

The recipe becomes the executable specification.

The Recipe Orchestrator converts the recipe into a DAG.

upload_001                  │                UNZIP                  │       ┌──────────┼──────────┐       ▼          ▼          ▼   machine01  machine02  production       │          │          │       └────┬─────┘          │            ▼                │          APPEND             │            │                │            └───────┬────────┘                    ▼                   JOIN                    │                    ▼              NORMALIZATION                    │                    ▼              VALIDATION

This makes the Compiler compatible with the existing Data Studio DAG architecture.

The Compiler should produce a canonical representation rather than merely a CSV.

Recommended structure:

AI-ConneX Unified Industrial Dataset│├── Dataset Metadata│├── Entity Information│├── Timestamp│├── Measurements│├── Events│├── Operational Variables│├── Labels / Targets│├── Units│├── Data Quality│└── Provenance

Every compiled dataset should have metadata similar to:

{  "dataset_id": "ACX-DS-000001",  "source_count": 7,  "compiled_at": "2026-08-14T10:30:00Z",  "schema_version": "1.0",  "row_count": 1845023,  "column_count": 27,  "operations": [    "UNZIP",    "APPEND",    "JOIN",    "NORMALIZE"  ],  "quality_status": "PASS"}

Every transformation should create lineage.

Source File    ↓Source Dataset    ↓Operation    ↓Intermediate Dataset    ↓Operation    ↓Unified Dataset

Example:

{  "operation_id": "OP-00042",  "operation": "JOIN",  "inputs": [    "machine_data.csv",    "production.xlsx"  ],  "keys": [    "machine_id",    "timestamp"  ],  "output": "dataset_stage_03"}

The Compiler should not have only:

SUCCESSFAILURE

Recommended states:

RECEIVEDINSPECTINGWAITING_FOR_AGENTPLAN_READYVALIDATINGEXECUTINGVALIDATING_OUTPUTCOMPILEDWARNINGNEEDS_CONFIRMATIONQUARANTINEDFAILED

Language:Python 3.13.14API:FastAPI 0.141.1Validation:Pydantic 2.13.1Data processing:Polars 1.43.0SQL / analytical execution:DuckDB 1.5.5Columnar format:Apache Arrow / PyArrow 25.0.0Excel:openpyxl 3.1.5HTTP multipart:python-multipart 0.0.32Environment/package manager:uv 0.11.33Container:DockerTesting:pytestStatic analysis:RuffType checking:mypy or pyrightStructured logging:structlog / standard loggingAgent orchestration:LangGraph or an equivalent internal state-machine layerObject storage:S3-compatible storageMetadata database:PostgreSQLCache:RedisObservability:OpenTelemetry + Prometheus-compatible metrics

The versions should be locked in the project lockfile rather than allowing floating production dependencies.

Polars is recommended for the primary dataframe engine because the Compiler is expected to process potentially large industrial datasets.

Its columnar execution model is well suited to:

filtering

projection

joins

aggregations

transformations

lazy execution

For extremely large datasets, the Compiler should avoid loading the entire dataset into RAM unnecessarily.

DuckDB becomes the SQL execution layer.

It is particularly useful for:

CSVParquetArrowlarge local datasetsjoinsaggregationsSQL transformations

It can complement Polars rather than replacing it.

Recommended division:

Polars→ dataframe transformationsDuckDB→ analytical SQL / large joins / file queryingPyArrow→ columnar interchange

FastAPI exposes Compiler functionality to:

Chatbot

Data Studio UI

internal orchestration

future external integrations

It also provides OpenAPI-based API documentation.

Pydantic should define the contracts between:

Chatbot → CompilerCompiler → Agent HelperAgent Helper → CompilerCompiler → Profiler

This prevents loosely structured JSON from moving between components.

The Agent Helper should ideally operate as a bounded state machine:

DISCOVER   ↓UNDERSTAND   ↓PROPOSE   ↓VALIDATE   ↓REVISE   ↓FINALIZE

This is safer than an unconstrained autonomous agent.

Minimum:

CPU:4 coresRAM:16 GBStorage:100 GB free SSDOS:Ubuntu 24.04 / Windows 11 / equivalentPython:3.13.xNetwork:Internet for package/model/API access

Recommended:

CPU:8+ coresRAM:32 GBSSD:500 GB+Network:1 Gbps

For a small industrial deployment:

8 vCPU32 GB RAM500 GB SSD

For larger workloads:

16–32 vCPU64–128 GB RAMNVMe SSDobject storagePostgreSQLRedis

The Compiler should be horizontally scalable because ingestion jobs can be asynchronous.

The Compiler itself does not fundamentally require a GPU.

The Agent Helper may use:

cloud LLM

or:

local LLM

depending on deployment.

Therefore:

Compiler:CPU-firstAgent Helper:CPU / GPU / cloud dependent

This is important for industrial edge deployments.

Example:

APP_ENV=developmentCOMPILER_MAX_UPLOAD_GB=20COMPILER_MAX_ARCHIVE_GB=20COMPILER_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED_GB=100COMPILER_MAX_FILES=10000COMPILER_MAX_ARCHIVE_DEPTH=5WORKSPACE_ROOT=/data/aiconnex/workspacesOBJECT_STORE_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000OBJECT_STORE_BUCKET=aiconnex-dataPOSTGRES_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/aiconnexREDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0AGENT_HELPER_MODE=hybridAGENT_CONFIDENCE_AUTO=0.90AGENT_CONFIDENCE_CONFIRM=0.75DEFAULT_TIMEZONE=UTCMAX_JOIN_EXPANSION_FACTOR=10ENABLE_PROVENANCE=trueENABLE_AUDIT_LOG=true

Secrets should never be committed into Git.

The Compiler API should expose a small set of stable contracts.

Recommended endpoints:

POST   /api/v1/compiler/jobsGET    /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}POST   /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}/planPOST   /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}/executeGET    /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}/reportGET    /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}/lineageGET    /api/v1/compiler/jobs/{job_id}/outputPOST   /api/v1/compiler/inspectPOST   /api/v1/compiler/validate

This is one of the most important interfaces in AI-ConneX.

The Chatbot should not send an arbitrary natural-language string only.

It should send:

USER INTENT+INPUT ASSETS+CONTEXT+DOMAIN+OBJECTIVE+CONSTRAINTS

Example:

{  "request_id": "REQ-00001",  "conversation": {    "conversation_id": "CONV-1001",    "turn_id": 12  },  "intent": {    "text": "Combine all the machine data and production records so they can be used for predictive maintenance.",    "task": "DATA_PREPARATION"  },  "domain": {    "name": "manufacturing"  },  "assets": [    {      "asset_id": "A001",      "name": "machine_data.zip",      "location": "object://uploads/A001"    },    {      "asset_id": "A002",      "name": "production.xlsx",      "location": "object://uploads/A002"    }  ],  "constraints": {    "preserve_original": true,    "require_provenance": true  }}

This object becomes the input to the Compiler.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 58. What the Compiler Receives From Chatbot
sections.content: The Compiler receives five conceptual inputs:

sections.heading_text: 1. User Intent2. Data Assets3. Industrial Context4. Constraints5. Expected Objective
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 1. User Intent2. Data Assets3. Industrial Context4. Constraints5. Expected Objective
sections.content:
Example:

User:"Use these files to prepare a dataset for predictive maintenance."Compiler receives:Intent:predictive maintenance preparationAssets:machine_data.zipmaintenance.xlsxsensor.csvDomain:manufacturingConstraints:preserve original datamaintain lineage

The Compiler gives the Agent Helper a controlled discovery package.

{  "job_id": "JOB-001",  "assets": [    {      "asset_id": "A001",      "format": "csv",      "rows": 120000,      "columns": [        {          "name": "Machine_ID",          "dtype": "string"        },        {          "name": "Time",          "dtype": "datetime"        },        {          "name": "Temp",          "dtype": "float"        }      ]    }  ]}

The Agent does not need the entire raw dataset.

It should generally receive:

metadata+schema+statistics+small representative samples

This reduces data leakage and LLM cost.

This is the second most important interface.

The Compiler does not simply send:

clean.csv

to the Data Profiler.

It should send:

UNIFIED DATASET+CANONICAL SCHEMA+DATASET METADATA+QUALITY REPORT+PROVENANCE+TRANSFORMATION RECIPE+STATISTICS

sections.heading_text: 63. What Data Profiler Should NOT Need to Do
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 63. What Data Profiler Should NOT Need to Do
sections.content:
The Data Profiler should not have to figure out:

Is this ZIP?Should these files be joined?Should these files be appended?What is the correct encoding?What was the original file?Which timestamp is equivalent?

That is the Compiler’s responsibility.

The Profiler should begin with:

What is the statistical and structural quality of this already-unified dataset?

This creates clean separation of responsibilities.

tables:
| Function | Compiler | Data Profiler |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File detection | ✓ |  |
| ZIP extraction | ✓ |  |
| Excel parsing | ✓ |  |
| Schema discovery | ✓ | ✓ |
| Dataset joining | ✓ |  |
| Dataset appending | ✓ |  |
| Dataset merging | ✓ |  |
| Type normalization | ✓ |  |
| Timestamp normalization | ✓ |  |
| Unit normalization | ✓ |  |
| Provenance | ✓ |  |
| Row statistics | Basic | ✓ |
| Distribution analysis | Basic | ✓ |
| Outlier analysis |  | ✓ |
| Missing-value analysis | Basic | ✓ |
| Correlation analysis |  | ✓ |
| ML readiness |  | ✓ |
| Feature engineering |  | Later stage |

sections.content:
For internal processing, the recommended primary output is:

Parquet

rather than CSV.

Why:

columnarcompressedtypedefficientlarge-data friendlyArrow compatibleDuckDB compatiblePolars compatible

CSV can still be offered as an export option.

The Compiler should produce:

dataset.parquetschema.jsonmetadata.jsonrecipe.jsonlineage.jsonquality_report.jsoncompiler_report.json

Optional:

preview.csvsample.parquethuman_readable_report.html

incoming/    ↓quarantine/    ↓extracted/    ↓discovered/    ↓intermediate/    ↓unified/    ↓profiler/

Original input must be preserved separately.

If one file is corrupt:

machine_01.csv  ✓machine_02.csv  ✓machine_03.csv  ✗machine_04.csv  ✓

the entire job should not necessarily crash.

The Compiler can report:

3 files processed1 file quarantined

and either:

continue

or:

request confirmation

depending on the user’s objective.

Bad or suspicious inputs should move to:

data/quarantine/

with:

reasontimestamphashoriginal locationsecurity scan resultparser errorjob ID

Example:

{  "asset_id": "A004",  "status": "QUARANTINED",  "reason": "Malformed XLSX archive",  "sha256": "...",  "job_id": "JOB-001"}

Example:

compiler:  output_format: parquet  preserve_original: true  enable_provenance: truesecurity:  max_upload_gb: 20  max_archive_gb: 20  max_uncompressed_gb: 100  max_files: 10000  max_archive_depth: 5join:  max_expansion_factor: 10  require_key_validation: true  allow_many_to_many: falseagent:  auto_execute_threshold: 0.90  confirmation_threshold: 0.75  max_retries: 3time:  canonical_timezone: UTCstorage:  intermediate_format: parquet

The Compiler should avoid:

df = read_everything_into_memory()

for large industrial datasets.

Instead use:

lazy executionstreamingchunked ingestioncolumn projectionpredicate pushdownParquetDuckDBPolars

Large files should be processed incrementally where possible.

Dataset fingerprints should be calculated.

Example:

SHA-256(file)

If the same file is submitted again:

same hash+same compiler version+same configuration

the Compiler may reuse an existing compiled artifact.

This reduces unnecessary processing.

Every compilation should record:

compiler versionrecipe versionschema versionconfiguration versioninput hashesagent plan versionparser versionsexecution timestamp

Therefore:

Same input+same recipe+same Compiler version+same configuration

should produce reproducible results wherever deterministic execution is possible.

The Compiler is exposed to arbitrary industrial uploads, so it must be treated as an untrusted-input processing service.

Required controls:

authenticationauthorizationfile-size limitsarchive limitspath traversal protectionmalware scanningsandboxed parsingresource limitstimeout limitsnetwork isolationaudit loggingencryptionsecure temporary storagesecret management

AI-ConneX should design the Compiler around controls that can support:

ISO/IEC 27001IEC 62443ISO 9001ISO/IEC 27701India DPDP ActGDPR where applicable

However:

Designing for these controls is not the same as being certified or legally compliant.

Formal compliance requires organizational policies, audits, evidence, risk assessments and certification/legal review.

For industrial environments, IEC 62443 should be treated as particularly important because AI-ConneX may eventually interact with:

OT networksSCADAPLC environmentsMESindustrial machinesedge devices

The Compiler itself should preferably remain separated from direct machine-control paths.

Recommended architecture:

OT Network     │     │ controlled gateway     ▼AI-ConneX ingestion boundary     │     ▼Compiler

The Compiler should not directly issue machine-control commands.

Recommended:

TLS in transitAES-256 or equivalent encryption at restRBACtenant isolationaudit logsretention policiesdata deletiondata lineage

Sensitive data should not automatically be transmitted to external LLM APIs.

The Agent Helper should generally receive:

schemastatisticsrepresentative samplesmetadata

instead of:

entire industrial dataset

unless explicitly required.

This is both:

security+cost+latency

optimization.

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 79. Compliance Evidence Generated by Compiler
sections.content:
Every job should produce evidence such as:

This forms the foundation of an audit trail.
AI-CONNEX-DS-COMPILER-REPORT-001
Chatbot   ↓Data Studio Compiler   ↓Data Profiler

This report certifies the processing state and evidence produced by the Compiler.

It is not a legal compliance certificate.

Example:

Possible final statuses:

The most important state is:

READY_FOR_PROFILER

This means the Compiler has successfully completed its responsibilities.

The Compiler should only output:

READY_FOR_PROFILER

when:

✓ input identified✓ files safely extracted✓ schemas discovered✓ transformation plan validated✓ joins validated✓ schema harmonized✓ timestamps normalized✓ units resolved where required✓ output written✓ output readable✓ provenance recorded✓ lineage recorded✓ report generated

sections.heading_text: 90. What the Compiler Guarantees to the Profiler
sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > 90. What the Compiler Guarantees to the Profiler
sections.content:
The Compiler’s contract with Data Profiler should effectively be:

“I have converted the user’s heterogeneous industrial inputs into a structurally valid, traceable, canonical dataset. You can now concentrate on profiling its statistical and ML-readiness characteristics.”

The Profiler can then start its work.

The complete Stage-1 pipeline is:

INDUSTRIAL USER                               │                               ▼                           JANE                         CHATBOT                               │                               │                    Intent + Data Assets                               │                               ▼                    ┌───────────────────┐                    │ DATA COMPILER     │                    └─────────┬─────────┘                              │                     File Detection                              │                     ZIP Extraction                              │                    Dataset Discovery                              │                              ▼                    ┌───────────────────┐                    │ AGENT HELPER      │                    └─────────┬─────────┘                              │                     Transformation Plan                              │                              ▼                    Plan Validation                              │                              ▼                    Recipe Generation                              │                              ▼                       DAG Execution                              │             ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐             ▼                ▼                ▼           APPEND            JOIN             MERGE             │                │                │             └────────────────┼────────────────┘                              ▼                    Schema Harmonization                              │                    Type Normalization                              │                   Timestamp Normalization                              │                      Unit Normalization                              │                         Validation                              │                        Provenance                              │                              ▼                 AI-CONNEX UNIFIED DATA                              │                    + schema.json                    + metadata.json                    + lineage.json                    + recipe.json                    + quality_report.json                              │                              ▼                    ┌───────────────────┐                    │   DATA PROFILER   │                    └───────────────────┘

The Compiler’s innovation is not:

“We support CSV, Excel and ZIP.”

That alone is not innovative.

The real AI-ConneX innovation is:

The system accepts industrial data in the form in which the industrial user already possesses it, understands relationships between heterogeneous datasets, determines the appropriate transformation strategy with an Agent Helper, validates that strategy deterministically, executes it as a DAG, preserves provenance, and delivers a canonical dataset to downstream AI systems.

That is substantially more powerful.

sections.heading_text: 93. Compiler as an Industrial Data Abstraction Layer

sections.content:
The Compiler effectively hides:

file formatsschemasencodingjoinsmergestimestampsunitsdata typesdata lineageETL complexity

sections.section_path: DOC-SPEC-001 > Phase R7 — Autonomous Data Engineering
sections.content: detectunderstandplanvalidateexecutemonitorlearn

The Data Studio Compiler should ultimately implement this principle:

DON'T ASK THE INDUSTRIALIST                         TO FIX THE DATA.                              ↓                   LET AI-ConneX UNDERSTAND IT.                              ↓                      AGENT HELPER                       REASONS ABOUT IT                              ↓                         COMPILER                     VALIDATES + EXECUTES                              ↓                       UNIFIED DATA                              ↓                       DATA PROFILER                              ↓                         ML STUDIO

The Compiler therefore acts as the industrial data translation and compilation boundary of AI-ConneX.

Its responsibility ends when the heterogeneous industrial input has become a validated, canonical, provenance-preserving dataset that Data Profiler can consume without needing to understand the original file-format chaos.

The AI-ConneX Data Studio Compiler Stage-1 is considered complete when the system can take:

one or more arbitrary supported industrial data assets

and automatically:

✓ identify formats✓ safely extract archives✓ inspect datasets✓ discover schemas✓ identify candidate keys✓ identify timestamps✓ identify units✓ detect schema relationships✓ determine append/join/merge requirements✓ use Agent Helper for ambiguous cases✓ validate the proposed plan✓ construct a DAG✓ execute transformations✓ prevent dangerous joins✓ normalize the canonical schema✓ normalize timestamps✓ resolve units where possible✓ detect duplicates✓ preserve source data✓ maintain provenance✓ generate REPORT_1✓ generate unified Parquet✓ generate schema metadata✓ generate lineage metadata✓ provide a clean input contract to Data Profiler

The final handoff is:

COMPILER OUTPUT                         │        ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐        ▼                ▼                ▼   Unified Data       Metadata         Lineage     Parquet             │                │        │                │                │        └────────────────┼────────────────┘                         ▼                 REPORT_1 / QUALITY                         │                         ▼                  DATA PROFILER

That is the formal boundary between Data Studio’s Compiler stage and the Data Profiler stage.
